module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-clock synchronous supervisory top that decodes a compact 64-bit configuration window, tracks one outstanding external surrogate transaction, and arbitrates between request issuance, response validation, command application, timeout handling, and fallback command generation.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use a simple encoded FSM with the required IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, FALLBACK, and TIMEOUT states. Configuration writes update compact control registers synchronously. A request_event initiates one request transaction when mode is enabled and no outstanding request is active. The top tracks request_tag, request age, watchdog count, freshness limit, clamp bounds, profile selection, and hold-last-good policy, then routes validated data to the safety stage and status outputs.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain one outstanding transaction context with request_tag, issue-time counter, and fault/status latches. Transition from IDLE to ISSUE_REQUEST on accepted request_event, then to WAIT_RESPONSE until either a valid response is accepted, a timeout occurs, or a validation failure is detected. Use VALIDATE_RESPONSE as the checking point before APPLY_COMMAND. Enter FALLBACK or TIMEOUT on invalid, stale, late, malformed, or missing responses, and recover to IDLE after fault handling when allowed by the handshake policy.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive req_valid/req_data as the outbound request stream, rsp_ready as the response-side ready, and act_cmd_valid/act_cmd_data as the final actuator stream. Only assert act_cmd_valid after validation and clamping, or when deterministic fallback is intentionally selected. Keep all top-level outputs under the specified width limits and ensure each output has a real RTL driver.
ownership_notes: Owns top-level configuration capture and 64-bit register readback.
Owns external transport direction compliance for request and response streams.
Owns transaction supervision, timeout, stale detection, and fault latching.
Owns final status bit generation for busy, request_pending, response_valid, stale_detected, timeout_detected, clamp_applied, fallback_active, and fault_latched.
Does not expose wide geometry, mesh, pressure-field, flow-field, or tensor ports.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_request_packer
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Compact bounded formatter that turns control metadata into a fixed-width 128-bit request packet using only small registers and combinational packing logic.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Accept a request_event only when enabled and the supervisor permits launch. Capture the current request_tag and metadata snapshot, then hold req_valid until req_ready completes the outbound handshake. Increment or otherwise advance request_tag on each accepted request so stale, duplicated, or out-of-order responses can be detected later.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use minimal request-hold state: idle, packet-present, and handshake-complete behavior is sufficient. No complex FSM is implied beyond preserving the packet until accepted.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Emit req_valid and req_data as the outbound request transport. Encode request_tag, geometry_descriptor_id, stream_velocity_mps, profile_selector, and health_status_bits into the bounded 128-bit record. Provide request_issued_pulse and request_tag_out for supervisory tracking.
ownership_notes: Does not implement physics inference or solver behavior.
Does not infer large payload FIFOs or flatten bulk storage into registers.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_response_guard
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Compact validator and watchdog manager that parses the incoming 128-bit response stream and compares it against the outstanding transaction context.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Accept rsp_valid data only when the request_tag matches the outstanding request and the response age is within the configured freshness window. Count request age from issue to acceptance. Force timeout detection when the watchdog limit is exceeded. Reject malformed, stale, duplicate, or out-of-order packets and raise fault indicators accordingly.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use a small validation sequence around the response handshake: observe, compare, qualify, and either accept or reject. No large FSM is required beyond handshake-driven checking and timeout supervision.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive rsp_ready back to the external service, and produce response_valid, stale_detected, timeout_detected, fault_detected, validated_request_tag, and a bounded validated_command candidate only after acceptance.
ownership_notes: Owns response acceptance, freshness checking, and timeout detection.
Owns rejection of stale or mismatched packets.
Does not expose surrogate tensors or internal model details.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_safety_fallback
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Safety and command-finalization stage that clamps accepted commands to configured bounds and replaces invalid traffic with a deterministic fallback command when faults are latched.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: When command_valid_in is asserted and no fault is present, clamp validated_command to cmd_min_bound/cmd_max_bound before presenting it to the actuator. When fault_latched is asserted, select a conservative deterministic fallback profile based on configuration or a hardcoded default. Optionally retain the last known good command only if hold_last_good_enable is explicitly set.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use minimal internal retention for last_good_command_out and the current final command choice. The behavior is primarily combinational or one-cycle registered, with no need for a complex FSM.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive act_cmd_valid only for validated-and-clamped commands or intentional fallback output, and drive act_cmd_data with the final bounded command. Assert clamp_applied when saturation occurs and fallback_active when fallback output is selected.
ownership_notes: Owns final actuator command selection and clamping.
Owns deterministic fallback behavior on faults.

fsm_intent: The top-level FSM is intentionally simple and encoded rather than elaborate.
IDLE waits for configuration enable and a request_event.
ISSUE_REQUEST launches exactly one compact request packet.
WAIT_RESPONSE monitors the outstanding transaction for either a valid response, stale data, or timeout.
VALIDATE_RESPONSE checks request_tag match, age freshness, and response integrity.
APPLY_COMMAND forwards the validated command to the safety/fallback stage for clamping and presentation.
FALLBACK emits a deterministic conservative command when a fault or invalid response is detected.
TIMEOUT is entered when the watchdog exceeds the configured limit and then hands off to fallback recovery.
The FSM must not deadlock; after fault handling it returns to IDLE or an equivalent ready-to-accept state.
datapath_intent: Inputs captured into compact configuration state include mode enable, watchdog limit, freshness limit, command min/max clamp bounds, geometry descriptor ID, control profile selection, and hold-last-good policy.
Runtime metadata includes stream_velocity_mps and health_status_bits, both forwarded into request packaging.
An outstanding request context stores request_tag and age/watchdog counters.
The request packet is fixed-width at 128 bits and contains only bounded metadata needed by the external surrogate service.
The response parser extracts only compact command-relevant data and validates it against the outstanding request context.
The final command path clamps the accepted command to safe bounds before act_cmd_data is driven.
Fallback command selection uses configuration or a conservative default and remains within the 32-bit actuator interface.
No wide payload history, geometry, mesh, or tensor storage is implied in registers; any future bulk buffering would map to technology-neutral BRAM abstraction.
sequencing_notes: Configuration writes are synchronous and update internal control registers before subsequent request issuance.
A request_event is serviced only when the design is enabled and not already waiting on an outstanding transaction.
Request_tag is advanced on each accepted request so response matching can detect stale or duplicate packets.
Response acceptance occurs only after tag match and freshness checks succeed.
Command clamping happens before act_cmd_valid is asserted to the actuator interface.
Fault conditions force the design into fallback or timeout handling without leaving the actuator output unprotected.
Optional hold-last-good behavior is applied only when explicitly configured; otherwise the deterministic fallback command is used.
Reset synchronously clears outstanding transaction state, status latches, and valid handshakes to a safe default.
timing_notes: A single synchronous clock domain is assumed for the controller, request packer, response guard, and safety/fallback stage.
The watchdog counts from request issue to response acceptance and triggers fallback when the configured limit is exceeded.
The stale-data detector compares both age and request_tag before any response is accepted.
Command clamping may be combinational or one-cycle registered, but must not allow out-of-range values to reach act_cmd_data.
The transport handshakes follow the mandatory direction contract: request valid/data are outputs with ready as input, and response valid/data are inputs with ready as output.
The design should recover to IDLE or fallback promptly when the external service is late or unavailable.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
